title: Add jurisdictional KMS labels and RBAC eviction hook for residency-backed keys
author: Maya Patel
description: Context: Customers in heavily regulated geographies require stronger binding between a tenant's declared residency and the KMS resources used to encrypt their data, plus better operator guardrails to prevent accidental cross-jurisdiction key use. This PR implements a lightweight jurisdictional KMS labeling layer in the private installer and an RBAC eviction hook that automatically quarantines operator sessions that attempt to bind keys across pinned zones. Motivation: avoid manual post-install configuration, reduce operational errors during upgrades and cross-zone maintenance, and provide clear audit evidence for compliance reviews. What this changes: 1) installer/internal/kms/labeler.go - adds a deterministic label assignment for CMKs created during installer flow: labels include geo_zone, residency_profile, and origin (installer|imported). 2) installer/templates/kms-mapping.yaml - Helm template used to seed residency->KMS alias mappings for the control plane. 3) rbac/policies/eviction-hook.yaml - admission hook that enforces RBAC v2 eviction when a session requests a key outside the session's claimed locale. 4) audit/tombstone/writer.py - writes a short-lived 'residency_tombstone' audit entry on eviction with a hashed proof to help auditors correlate operator actions without leaking tenant identifiers. Design notes: - Labeling is additive and idempotent; existing keys are detected by fingerprint and annotated when imported. - The eviction hook consults the policy engine cache; fallbacks to deny if policy cannot be evaluated. - Tombstone entries are compact (SHA256 of claim + timestamp) and persisted to the audit forwarder with a residency tag; full claim material is not emitted. Migration and rollout: - Step 1 (canary): deploy labeler + template to canary installer (non-prod). Installer will run in dry-run mode to surface label mismatches in a report under /var/log/installer/residency-labeler.log. - Step 2 (soft-enforce): enable eviction hook in shadow mode; it will log but not evict. - Step 3 (enforce): switch eviction hook to enforce and enable tombstone writes. Rollback plan: revert helm values to disable eviction hook and remove labeler flag; tombstone writer is opt-in via config so it will stop emitting if disabled. Security considerations: keys are never moved; labels are metadata only. Tombstone entries are hashed and opt-in per customer. Test plan: unit tests for label deterministic mapping and admission logic; integration test (tests/integration/test-residency-kms.sh) simulates cross-zone operator session and asserts eviction + tombstone entry. CI: added integration matrix for region-pin=true in installer CI. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-1345) [x] unit tests added [x] integration tests added [x] helm values defaults updated [x] docs updated (operational notes) Related: builds on GEN-allocator work; complements platform RBAC v2 migration. Links: linear/ENG-1345 | docs/operational/residency-kms-mapping.md | tests/integration/test-residency-kms.sh

Add Helm template for residency -> KMS alias mapping
Add RBAC admission eviction hook and policy YAML
Add audit tombstone writer and integration test
review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Please confirm idempotency for imported keys and add test coverage for fingerprint collisions. Maya Patel: Added a collision test and described fallback behavior in code comments.

Neha Srinivasan: Concern — eviction could disrupt on-call ops during upgrades. Can we add a shadow mode and a rate limit for evictions? Maya Patel: Implemented shadow mode flag and a 1evict/min rate limiter with exponential backoff; documented in rollout notes.

Ravi Desai: Audit entry payload small but ensure forwarder retention policy won't drop tombstones early. Maya Patel: Coordinated with observability; tombstones will be forwarded to a separate retention namespace (residency-audit) for 90 days by default.
merge_outcome: squash and merge into main; PR merged after 2 approvals and green CI
release_notes: installer: introduce jurisdictional KMS labeling and RBAC eviction hook (opt-in by default). Enables compliance teams to pin KMS usage by tenant residency and provides audit tombstones for operator evictions. Not enabled for existing installs unless the residency flag is turned on. See docs/operational/residency-kms-mapping.md for migration steps.
